transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brings you here today?

Hi, yeah, thanks for seeing me. Um, I guess what finally made me make an appointment is that I just keep turning in these job applications—and my research notes, too—with these small but really embarrassing mistakes. Like, I'll completely mislabel an artwork date or just skip a question on a form entirely. And the frustrating part is that I honestly thought I had checked them. I'll sit there and proofread it and swear it's perfect, but then it's wrong. 

It's mostly for these gallery and museum jobs I'm applying to, since I just finished my bachelor's. The job market is just absolutely brutal right now. My friend Mark applied to literally forty places and ended up working at a plant nursery. Which is actually kind of cool, he gets a huge discount on monsteras and pothos, and I've been trying to get more into houseplants because my apartment is just so bare right now. I bought this one fern last week, but I think I'm overwatering it because the leaves are getting weirdly yellow at the tips... 

Wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, the applications. Yeah, just... making really dumb mistakes on my paperwork even after I check them. So, yeah, that's why I'm here.
Have you been feeling down or losing interest in things you usually enjoy, like taking care of your plants or applying for jobs?

No, I wouldn't say I'm feeling down. I mean, nobody really *enjoys* applying for jobs, right? But I'm still interested in things. Like the plants—I'm actually really excited about them. I was just looking online for some new ceramic pots for that fern, because the plastic one it came in is just so ugly and it doesn't drain well. 

There's this really cool pottery studio downtown that offers classes, and I was actually thinking about taking one. My mom used to do pottery when I was a kid, and we had all these weird, lopsided bowls around the house. She tried to make a teapot once and the spout completely fell off in the kiln. It was hilarious, we ended up using it to hold spare change in the kitchen for years. I think my dad finally threw it out when they moved, which is kind of a shame. 

But anyway, what was the question? Oh, right, feeling down. No, I don't feel depressed or anything like that. Just really frustrated about making all those stupid mistakes on my paperwork.
Can you describe how you organize your job applications and how you approach proofreading them? Do you find yourself getting distracted easily during that process?

Um, organizing them... I try to keep a spreadsheet, honestly. I have it color-coded and everything. But when I actually sit down at my desk to work on them, or to proofread my cover letters, it's like... I just can't stay on track. Like, if I'm trying to read through my writing, and there's a siren outside, or I hear someone talking in the hallway, my brain just instantly goes there. Or even if it's completely quiet, I'll just have a random thought about, like, an idea for a museum exhibit. 

Actually, I had this really cool idea the other day for an exhibit about the history of ordinary objects, like spoons. You'd be surprised how much the shape of a spoon has changed over the centuries. Did you know the Romans used these really ornate silver spoons with pointed ends so they could eat snails? They called them cochlearia. I went down this massive Wikipedia rabbit hole about Roman dining habits for, like, three hours the other night. They used to eat lying down on these slanted couches, which sounds incredibly uncomfortable for digestion, if you ask me. I always get heartburn if I lay down too soon after eating pizza. Especially the pepperoni one from that place down the street, it's so greasy... 

Wait, sorry. The applications. Yeah, so, a siren or a random thought about an exhibit will pull me away, and like twenty minutes will go by before I even notice I stopped proofreading. It's really annoying.
Do you find yourself getting distracted like this in other parts of your life, like when you're reading, having conversations, or doing other tasks around the house?

Um, yeah, I guess so. Like, if I'm trying to read a book, I end up reading the same paragraph over and over because I just drift off. I was trying to read this book on art history the other day, and it mentioned something about pigment mixing in the Renaissance. And then I started thinking about how they used to make ultramarine blue out of crushed lapis lazuli. It was crazy expensive, like, more expensive than gold. They had to import it all the way from Afghanistan. 

Actually, I have this friend who went to Afghanistan a few years ago for some NGO work. She brought back these incredible photos of the mountains there. She's a photographer, and she uses this vintage film camera. I've always wanted to get into film photography. There's just something so authentic about it, you know? The graininess, the colors. Digital just feels too... perfect sometimes. I was looking at cameras on eBay last night, actually. 

But, um... what did you ask me? Oh, right, other parts of my life. I don't really know. I guess I haven't really thought about it happening during conversations or chores, just mostly when I'm trying to read or do my applications.
Do you often feel restless, as if you can't sit still for long, or do you find yourself needing to be constantly doing something?

Um, restless? No, not really. I mean, I can sit still just fine. I don't feel like I have to be running around or constantly doing things. Actually, I can sit for hours if I'm doing something I like. Like the other day, I sat on my couch for almost four hours straight just watching this documentary series about deep-sea creatures. 

It is wild what lives down there. There's this one fish, the barreleye fish, and it has a completely transparent head. Like, you can see its brain and everything. And its eyes are these glowing green orbs that look straight up through its own head to see shadows of prey above it. It's so weird. It kind of made me think about how little we actually know about the ocean. We've mapped more of the surface of Mars than we have of our own ocean floor. I was telling my roommate about it, and he said we should get a fish tank. But I don't know, keeping fish seems like a lot of work. You have to monitor the pH levels and clean the algae... my cousin had a tank when we were kids, and he got this really aggressive beta fish that ended up eating all the other fish. He named it Terminator. 

But yeah, anyway... no, I don't feel restless or anything like that. I'm pretty okay just sitting.
Have you noticed any days where you feel particularly down, hopeless, or where even things you usually enjoy, like plants or art, feel less rewarding than normal?

Um, down or hopeless? No, I don't think so. I mean, I still really like all my plants and everything. I actually just repotted my Monstera yesterday because it was getting way too big for its old pot. It's crazy how fast those things grow if you give them enough indirect light. I use this specific soil mix with a lot of perlite and orchid bark so the roots can breathe. 

Did you know that in the wild, Monsteras actually climb up trees? They have these aerial roots that just latch onto the bark. I saw this amazing picture of one in a rainforest in Costa Rica, and the leaves were like three feet wide. I'd love to go to Costa Rica someday. They have all these eco-lodges where you can stay right in the jungle and wake up to the sound of howler monkeys. My dad went there on a business trip once, but he didn't even get to see any monkeys because he was stuck in conference rooms the whole time. Which sounds awful. I could never do a job where I'm just sitting in a beige room all day. That's why I'm trying to find something in a museum or a gallery, you know? 

But, uh, no, I don't feel depressed or anything like that. I still enjoy my stuff.
